newsitem.title: USA: Hasbro to close N.Y. Playskool plant.
newsitem.headline: Hasbro to close N.Y. Playskool plant.

text.p: Hasbro Inc. said Wednesday it will close its Amsterdam, N.Y. manufacturing facility, which employs 400 people, at the end of November.
Production of Playskool toys that took place there will be moved to a facility in Texas, Hasbro said.
Hasbro said it was developing severance packages for all its employees and will establish a centre to retrain and prepare laid-off Hasbro workers for re-employment.
The company was not immediately available to say if a charge would be involved with the plant closing.

"After much deliberation and a careful analysis of our manufacturing capacity, we reached this difficult but necessary decision," Jerry Ligon, president of Hasbro's manufacturing service group, said in a statement.
Ligon said competition in the toy business required the Pawtucket, R.I.-based company to adjust its production load at its North American plants.
Hasbro acquired the plant from Coleco Industries Inc. in 1988. Hasbro's stock rose 62.5 cents to $37.75 on the American Stock Exchange.
